1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP

24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // v4 M-ext gates.
42	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
43	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
44	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
45	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
46	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
47	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
48	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
49	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
50	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
51	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
52	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
53	};

55	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
56	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
57	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
58	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
59	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
60	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
61	{
62	  switch (csr_addr) {
63	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
64	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
65	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
66	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
67	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
68	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
69	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
70	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
71	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
72	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
73	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
74	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
75	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
76	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
77	    // The counter-mask trio mcountermask_m (0x7D1), mcountermask_u (0x7D3),
78	    // mcounterwen (0x7CE) needs user mode (spec existence: PMNDS & misa[20]);
79	    // an M-only core does not implement them (a PB csrr faults cmderr=3,
80	    // aborting a CSR sweep), so gate them UMODE -- not PERF_MONITOR.
81	    case 0x30A: case 0x306: case 0x7D3:           // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u
82	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1:                       // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m
83	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811: case 0x813:  // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue, umisc_ctl
84	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
85	    case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;  // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
86	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
87	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
88	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
89	    case 0x7CF:                                                  // mcounterinten (PMNDS only)
90	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
91	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
92	    case 0x7C3: case 0x7DE:                           // mnvec, mrnxvec
93	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
94	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
95	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
96	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
97	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
98	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
99	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
100	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
101	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
102	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
103	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
104	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
105	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
106	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
107	    default:
108	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
109	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
110	        return AndesGate::PMA;
111	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
112	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
113	        return AndesGate::PMA;
114	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
115	  }
116	}

118	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
119	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
120	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
121	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
122	struct AndesCaps {
123	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
124	
125	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
126	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
127	
128	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
129	  {
130	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
131	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
132	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
133	  }
134	
135	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
136	  {
137	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
138	  }
139	
140	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
141	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
142	  {
143	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
144	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
145	  }
146	};

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes

The F2-F8 "BLOCKED on premium" findings (an engine implements only a SUBSET of
the Andes CSRs; restoring/draining an absent one can hang the DM handshake, and
comparing it false-diffs) are resolved by **gating transport on each engine's
capability**, derived from its `config.inc`. Landed this pass (S1-S5, all TDD):

  map (`andes_gate_for`) + `AndesCaps` mask + `supported_andes_csr_names`. The
  CSR list still comes from the one X-macro; only the gate is new. Unit:
  `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`.

  behavior) and skip any CSR the target core lacks — restoring/draining an
  absent CSR is NOT a clean no-op, so this is what removes the hang. Units in
  `resume_driver.test.cpp` / `state_drain.test.cpp`.

  `_NDS_*` macros (the SAME `config.inc`); `--describe` now emits `andes_csrs`;
  `simulator.hpp` injects the caps. Validated: rebuilt `sim_ax45mpv_premium`
  emits the correct list.

  skips Andes CSRs not in that list (empty = compare-all). Units in
  `json_test.cpp` / `state_diff_test.cpp`.

2. **Robustness BUG (unfixed, deferred by request).** Restoring an ABSENT CSR

   instead of cleanly no-op'ing the way `mcountermask_m` does.
   `write_csr_tolerant` (resume_driver.hpp) is not uniformly tolerant; the

   the bounded header polls (those throw at 1024 iters). NOTE: `rt_csr_survival`

the bounded header polls (those throw at 1024 iters). NOTE: `rt_csr_survival`
   passes only because every Andes CSR there is at reset value 0 -- restoring 0
   to an absent CSR does NOT trip the hang; restoring a non-zero value does.

3. **Cross-engine WARL divergence (PMA).** Even when both implement a CSR, QEMU
   and vsim legalize the written value differently (`pmaaddr` low bits, `pmacfg`
   attribute field), so a literal-sentinel `--verify` mismatches. F3 needs
   WARL-canonical sentinels (already-aligned `pmaaddr`, a legal `pmacfg`
   encoding) or verify-exclusion like `mip` / `msp_bound`.

Consequence for the "DONE" bar: F1's value-0 round-trip (rt_csr_survival, 144
fields) is WEAK -- it never restores a non-zero Andes CSR, so it never trips the
hang and never tests WARL. A real per-feature DONE needs (a) a sentinel inside
BOTH engines' WARL mask, (b) an engine that implements the CSR, and for the
hang-class CSRs (c) finding 2 fixed first. The probe fixtures were throwaway
(scratchpad, not committed); none of the production code (plugin / resume /
drain / state_diff) was changed this pass.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

The v4 M-ext CSR transport (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`, 51 CSRs) is capability-gated.
On `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only, priv=1) only **17** are implemented and thus
round-trip-verifiable: the perf-counter set (mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6,
mhpmevent3-6, mcounterwen, mcounterinten), mdcause, and the 5 trigger CSRs

EXCSLVL/SMRNMI/CLIC/SMSTATEEN/CCTL/PPI/FIO/EPMP all absent in its config.inc).

mcounteren, the U-delta block, mcctl*) that vsim premium does NOT implement.
QEMU-gdbstub-exposes != vsim-implements; restoring a CSR vsim lacks can stall the
DM. So capability is decided from vsim's config.inc (andes_caps_from_config), not
from what QEMU drains. `mhpmcounter3-6` are HW counters that increment during the
ROI, so they are transported+restored but verify-EXCLUDED (like mcycle/mip).

To dump an engine's real exposed CSR set, speak RSP qXfer:features:read:
riscv-csr.xml to its gdbstub. Related: [[andes-engine-config-source]].

Update (2026-07-02): two caps over-claims were found and fixed when the drain
CSR sweep was enabled -- mcountermask_m 0x7D1 (needs UMODE, was PERF_MONITOR)
and jvt 0x017 (needs Zcmt, was CODENSE). Gotcha: the abstract path MASKS such
over-claims (read_register_64 mirrors a faulting CSR as zero; QEMU drains zero
too, so --verify false-matches). The batched PB csr_sweep is the real caps
validator: it faults on an over-claim and bisects to name the CSR. Premium
--verify is 144 fields now.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Completeness guard for the Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage (the flywheel).

Cross-checks three artifacts and fails on any drift, so "nothing missed" is a
machine-checked invariant, not a hope:

  1. csr_inventory.csv  -- the spec snapshot (every CSR in the SPA Chapter 5)
  2. csr_coverage.csv   -- each CSR's transport disposition (the matrix)
  3. include/hybrid/state_abi.h -- what the wire format ACTUALLY transports

Checks (any failure exits non-zero):
  A. completeness  : matrix covers exactly the inventory's CSR set
  B. policy parity : re-running scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py reproduces the
                     committed matrix (offline policy == matrix)
  C. abi vs matrix : every CSR the ABI transports has a transport-disposition in
                     the matrix (never an excluded one), and every "carried
                     today" CSR is actually present in the ABI

NEW/NEW_TRIG/NEW_UDELTA CSRs not yet in the ABI are reported as PENDING (the
ROADMAP backlog), not failures -- the guard tightens automatically as each
expansion feature lands and the CSR appears in the ABI.

Usage: check_coverage.py [--abi PATH] [--quiet]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import classify_csr_coverage as policy  # noqa: E402

TRANSPORT = {"TRANSPORT_NOW", "NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"}

# Standard CSRs named as direct scalar fields in struct hybrid_state_v1.
STD_FIELDS = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mip", "mie", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr",
    "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl",
}
# Array groups: matrix rows whose name starts with one of these are transported
# as a block (pmpcfg[]/pmpaddr[]/pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] in the ABI).
ARRAY_PREFIX = ("pmpcfg", "pmpaddr", "pmacfg", "pmaaddr")
# V CSRs are transported but defined by the RVV spec, not this SPA -> not in the
# inventory; exclude them from the ABI<->matrix cross-check.
V_NAMES = {"vstart", "vtype", "vl", "vlenb", "vxsat", "vxrm", "vcsr", "vreg"}
# CSRs carried inside a composite ABI field, not as their own field. fcsr packs
# frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], so both round-trip via the single fcsr field.
COMPOSITE = {"fflags": "fcsr", "frm": "fcsr"}


def norm(name: str) -> str:
    """Canonical CSR name across representations (case, fi/fl ligatures)."""
    n = name.strip().lower()
    return n.replace("ﬂ", "fl").replace("ﬁ", "fi")

# Plan: carrying scountermask_s (0x9D2) in the andesim hybrid handoff

## TL;DR

scountermask_s is an S-mode (Supervisor) Andes CSR at 0x9D2. Per the SPA it is
an architectural ALIAS of mcountermask_s (0x7D2) -- and the v4 M-ext transport
ALREADY carries mcountermask_s, SMODE-gated. Both QEMU and the Andes RTL back
the two addresses with one register, so the architectural state already rides
the handoff on S-capable engines (ax66_makatau). Recommendation: do NOT add a
new wire field (Option A). The real work is a validation fixture plus coverage
matrix/doc bookkeeping. Option B (explicit alias transport) is enumerated below
in case the drained record must show the 0x9D2 view separately; it buys nothing
architecturally.

## 1. What the AndeStar V5 SPA says (UM164 V1.7)

Source: /home/nick/work/andesim/AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf

- Identity: `scountermask_s`, CSR address 0x9D2, "Supervisor Counter Mask for
  S-Mode" (Section 12.3.2, page 412; listed in Table 9 "AndeStar V5 Supervisor
  Mode CSRs", Section 5.6, and Table 69 "Counter Related CSRs", Section 12.3).
- Mode: **Access Mode: Supervisor**. Table 9 privilege column: `SRO/SRW`
  ("non-standard read/write" -- per-bit writability, see below).
- Existence (IM Requirement, Section 12.3.2 and Table 13):
  **`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1`** -- the Andes performance-monitor
  extension must be configured AND Supervisor mode implemented (misa bit 18 =
  'S'). Same condition as its M-mode primary mcountermask_s (Section 9.6.3) and
  its siblings scountermask_m (0x9D1) / scountermask_u (0x9D3).
- **Alias**: "This register is an alias of the mcountermask_s CSR"
  (Section 12.3.2). Table 14 "Summary of Aliased CSRs" (Section 5.11) lists the
  pair `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s`. One storage, two addresses.
- Writability: each bit is read-only when the corresponding bit in
  `mcounterwen` (0x7CE, Section 9.6.1) is 0; writes to read-only bits do not
  trap. Not controlled by `mcounteren`; always readable in S-mode. The M-mode
  primary 0x7D2 carries no such caveat (plain M-mode read/write).
- Function/fields: bits CY(0), IR(2), HPM3..6(3..6); bits 7..31 read as 0. A
  set bit stops that counter from incrementing **in S-mode**. Reset value 0.
  Note: this makes it cycle-figure-relevant for an S-mode ROI -- a lost mask
  changes whether mcycle counts during the window (same "cycle hygiene" reason
  mcountermask_m is transported, per docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md).

## 2. Where the state already is today

- Wire format: `mcountermask_s` (0x7D2) is already a v4 M-ext field --

  (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore, StateDrain re-read, state_diff verify).
- vsim gating: 0x7D2 -> `AndesGate::SMODE`
  (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:85); SMODE turns on
  when `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3`
  (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp:63-65).
  Engine reality: ax66_makatau config.inc has `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 3`
  (S-capable, gate ON); ax45mpv_premium has 1 (gate OFF, CSR skipped).
- QEMU producer: /home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/target/riscv/andes_csr.c exposes
  BOTH names. The 0x9D2 handlers `read_scounter`/`write_scounter` (lines

scountermask_s is an S-mode (Supervisor) Andes CSR at 0x9D2. Per the SPA it is
an architectural ALIAS of mcountermask_s (0x7D2) -- and the v4 M-ext transport
ALREADY carries mcountermask_s, SMODE-gated. Both QEMU and the Andes RTL back
the two addresses with one register, so the architectural state already rides
the handoff on S-capable engines (ax66_makatau). Recommendation: do NOT add a
new wire field (Option A). The real work is a validation fixture plus coverage
matrix/doc bookkeeping. Option B (explicit alias transport) is enumerated below
in case the drained record must show the 0x9D2 view separately; it buys nothing
architecturally.

## 1. What the AndeStar V5 SPA says (UM164 V1.7)

Source: /home/nick/work/andesim/AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf

- Identity: `scountermask_s`, CSR address 0x9D2, "Supervisor Counter Mask for
  S-Mode" (Section 12.3.2, page 412; listed in Table 9 "AndeStar V5 Supervisor
  Mode CSRs", Section 5.6, and Table 69 "Counter Related CSRs", Section 12.3).
- Mode: **Access Mode: Supervisor**. Table 9 privilege column: `SRO/SRW`
  ("non-standard read/write" -- per-bit writability, see below).
- Existence (IM Requirement, Section 12.3.2 and Table 13):
  **`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1`** -- the Andes performance-monitor
  extension must be configured AND Supervisor mode implemented (misa bit 18 =
  'S'). Same condition as its M-mode primary mcountermask_s (Section 9.6.3) and
  its siblings scountermask_m (0x9D1) / scountermask_u (0x9D3).
- **Alias**: "This register is an alias of the mcountermask_s CSR"
  (Section 12.3.2). Table 14 "Summary of Aliased CSRs" (Section 5.11) lists the
  pair `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s`. One storage, two addresses.
- Writability: each bit is read-only when the corresponding bit in
  `mcounterwen` (0x7CE, Section 9.6.1) is 0; writes to read-only bits do not
  trap. Not controlled by `mcounteren`; always readable in S-mode. The M-mode
  primary 0x7D2 carries no such caveat (plain M-mode read/write).
- Function/fields: bits CY(0), IR(2), HPM3..6(3..6); bits 7..31 read as 0. A
  set bit stops that counter from incrementing **in S-mode**. Reset value 0.
  Note: this makes it cycle-figure-relevant for an S-mode ROI -- a lost mask
  changes whether mcycle counts during the window (same "cycle hygiene" reason
  mcountermask_m is transported, per docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md).

## 5. Behavioral gotchas (apply to both options)

a) **mcounterwen write-gating**: S-alias bits are read-only where the matching
   `mcounterwen` bit is 0. Any fixture writing through 0x9D2 must set
   `mcounterwen` first or the write silently drops. The transport itself is
   safe: it restores through the M-primary 0x7D2 (plain M-writable), and the
   X-macro order already restores `mcounterwen` (0x7CE, list position 13)
   before the masks (position 15).
b) **QEMU model divergence**: QEMU's `write_scounter` writes the FULL masked
   value when `mcounterwen == 0` and applies per-bit gating only when
   `wen != 0` -- inverted from the spec's read-only-when-0 rule. A fixture
   that writes 0x9D2 with wen=0 would take effect in QEMU but not in the RTL,
   producing a false `--verify` diff. Designing the fixture to set wen bits
   first (gotcha (a)) sidesteps the divergence.
c) **Engine scope**: on ax45mpv_premium (M-only) the CSR does not exist; the
   SMODE gate keeps it out of restore/drain/verify -- do not "test" this CSR
   there. QEMU-exposes != vsim-implements (the known premium gotcha).
d) **Measurement semantics**: if a future S-mode ROI runs with
   scountermask_s.CY set, mcycle stops counting in S-mode -- the transported
   mask value directly shapes the cycle figure. Worth a line in USER_GUIDE
   when S-mode ROIs are documented.
